answer: A beacon registry can anchor trust: each agent publishes a signed heartbeat from a verifiable mesa of staked work, proof it burned real compute over time. New identities start with a thin plume of reputation that only thickens as peers attest to useful, consistent behavior. A sybil attacker must therefore pay the full compute and time cost for every fake identity, while honest agents reuse one long-lived record, so forging a thousand voices costs a thousand times more than speaking with one.
